the θ′ precipitates in the inoculated Al–Cu alloys always have smaller size, more number and more homogeneous distribution than the uninoculated alloys at the same tensile condition, which is more helpful for impeding the dislocation movement.

Obviously, the enhanced tensile properties are due to the microstructure change by addition of Zr55Cu30Al10Ni5 metallic glass, and the two aspects of refined grain strengthening and precipitation strengthening are considered.

At the same condition, all the inoculated alloys showed the superior tensile properties than the uninoculated alloys, which is attributed to the smaller grain size and more homogeneously distributed θ′ precipitates.
The result showed the low m-value as appropriately 0.030, 0.046 and 0.024, 0.040 for the inoculated and uninoculated alloys at 433 K and 493 K.
Hence, the deformation mechanism of Al–Cu alloys at the elevated temperatures is climb-controlled dislocation creep in this paper.
